answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 207 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 111 times the capital for one share. The umber report exposes the merge explicitly at each violet. Each collapsed cluster gets one tide weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds.
